MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  March 23, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:08p.m., on Monday, March 23, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.
PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Clerk Lamb McCarthy, Director of Parks and
Recreation Macias, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of
Public Works and Utilities Ahlen, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Chief of Police Kennedy, Assistant
Police Chief Seki, Lieutenant Castillo, Director of Library Services LohGuan, Director of Human
Resources Ko, Management Analyst – Sustainability Martel, Management Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

CEREMONIAL

1.  PROCLAMATION: RED CROSS MONTH – F2M26-3
  Mayor Maloney and the City Council proclaimed March, 2026 as RED CROSS MONTH in
  Alhambra and acknowledged the Red Cross for their support in the community

  Mayor Maloney presented the Red Cross Month proclamation to Maggie MAO with the
  Community Engagement & Partnership, Disaster Cycle Services division of the San
  Gabriel and Pomona Valley Chapter of the American Red Cross. Mr.. Ms. MAO thanked
  the City for their partnership in helping to promote fire safety awareness in the community.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS - F2M26-4

1) “Alhambra Citizens”, as a retired Police Sergeant, spoke against the lack of closed captioning
  services within Council Chambers and addressed fraud and waste in the Annual Action Plan
  and Los Angeles Housing services.

2) Chris Vasquez, 1645 S. Primrose Ave., spoke against parking citations he received despite
  possessing an annual parking permit.

3) Gary, 800 N. Monterey St., spoke regarding privacy and civil rights concerns Flock cameras
  in Alhambra, as it relates to federal immigration enforcement and requested the City to cancel
  their contract with Flock Safety in support of SB34 which prohibits local police from sharing
  license plate data with out of state agencies such as the Federal Immigration and Customs
  Enforcement (ICE).

4) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., spoke against the noise from the annual Lunar New Year
  event on Main Street, recalling the noise interference when the event was held on Valley Blvd.,
  and addressed loud music and noise from Pepe’s restaurant and F45 Training Gym at 428
  W. Main St.

Regular City Council Meeting Minutes — March 23, 2026  Page 1 of 10
 PRESENTATIONS
2.  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. R2M26-7 ENTITLED A RESOLUTION OF THE ALHAMBRA
  CITY COUNCIL REGARDING CITY RESPONSE TO FEDERAL CIVIL IMMIGRATION
  ACTIVITIES – F2M26-7, R2M26-7
  Mayor MALONEY and Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER, as the members of Council’s
  subcommittee, reported on their meetings with the community and other local agencies,
  made comments regarding the negative effects of federal immigration enforcement
  actions on the community, and discussed Council’s support of the Resolution to address
  changing immigration policies and action.

  Councilmember WANG asked for clarification regarding signage. Mr. MALONEY spoke
  regarding the provisions for “ICE Free Zones,” and directed staff to review signage used
  by other cities to delineate said zones. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER also spoke regarding
  the use of signage. Ms. WANG and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the types of
  signs for various locations. Councilmember LEE asked for clarification regarding the use
  of signs and the legal ramifications of the signs. Mr. MALONEY further discussed the
  intention of the signs to be used on private property as a statement denying permission to
  ICE to enter their property. Mr. MALONEY went on to discuss the development of the
  Resolution and changes made at the suggestion of the community.

  Public Comment: Mayor Maloney opened public communications, the following
  spoke:
  7) Anthony Pham
  1) Melissa Michelson
  8) Jamie Carter
  2) Lewis McCammon
  9) Jeffrey Gomez
  3) Victor
  10) Sawyer Brooks(Zoom)
  4) Alex Maltuh
  11) Robert Lopez (emailed comment)
  5) Rachel B.
  6) Shirley Tatsuno
  Discussion: Vice Mayor Andrade-Stadler expressed gratitude to the community and City
  Council for their support, affirming her endorsement of activism and the Resolution.
  Councilmember Wang and City Attorney Montes discussed issues related to schools and
  hospitals as private property, as well as ICE-Free Zones. Maza requested an amendment
  advocating for comprehensive federal immigration reform and shared his family’s history
  with reform efforts in the 1980s. Montes clarified the proposed amendment by adding Item
  11, calling for federal immigration reform, which was supported by Andrade-Stadler and
  Maloney.

  Councilmember Lee, who also supported federal reform, highlighted the limitations of local
  laws, recent incidents of injury, and supported provisions for masked enforcement agents.
  Mayor Maloney echoed the importance of public input, discussed recent events both
  locally and nationally, and expressed support for the Resolution. He also requested a
  minor typographical correction to a quote from a Senate Bill.

  After discussion, Montes proposed language for Item 11: "The City Council urges federal
  and state officials to enact comprehensive immigration reform that provides a clear path
  to legal residency and citizenship," which was approved. Andrade-Stadler addressed
  public comments concerning immigration enforcement in schools and clarified the
  procedures involved.

  Action Taken: City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-7 entitled: A Resolution of
  the Alhambra City Council Regarding City Response to Federal Civil Immigration
  Activities, with an amendment

Regular City Council Meeting Minutes — March 23, 2026  Page 2 of 10
   Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

RECESS & RECONVENE:  Mayor Maloney called for a brief recess at 7:43 p.m. and
reconvened with all members present at 7:50 p.m.

3.  ANNUAL BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS APPOINTMENTS – F2M26-29
  Assistant City Clerk Lamb McCarthy presented a staff report noting that all Board and
  Commission terms expire on March 23, 2026. The City Council should appoint or
  reappoint their representative, except for the Youth Commission, each seat can serve up
  to eight consecutive one-year terms. Appointments will run from March 23, 2026, to March
  22, 2027.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the end of term
  for Eric Garcia on the Planning Commission and thanked him for his service.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER requested to remove Ken Tang
  from the Human Relations Commission and to appoint Kristin Keenan, to appoint Henry
  Aviles to the Transportation Commission replacing Monica Calderon. This would leave a
  vacancy on the Parks and Recreation Commission. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER noted that
  she was uncertain about Katie Chan on Environmental Sustainability due to work
  scheduling, and uncertain about her Youth Commission appointees due to school
  scheduling.

  Councilmember LEE requested to reappoint all incumbent Board and Commission
  members. Councilmember MAZA made no changes. Councilmember WANG requested
  to remove Joyce Amaro from the Historic Preservation Commission upon her request.
  She made no other changes.

  Ms. WANG requested the Civic Service Application to become a Board or Commission
  member be updated to include a section to make a personal statement. City Attorney
  MONTES stated that staff would change the application. Ms. LEE requested additional
  information regarding the responsibilities for each Board and Commission and Mr.
  MALONEY provided clarification regarding Council’s last review and update to the
  ordinances pertaining to Boards and Commissions. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER requested
  a copy of the ordinances pertaining to Boards and Commissions be sent to Council for
  review. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER suggested that until the Human Relations Commission
  attains a full roster of appointments, that Council continue the subcommittee to review
  federal immigration enforcement actions.
  Action Taken:  The Mayor and each Councilperson announced his/her new
  appointments to the Arts & Cultural Events Commission, Civil Service Commission/Board
  of Appeals, Design Review Board, Environmental Sustainability Commission, HCDA
  Citizen Advisory Committee, Historic Preservation Commission, Human Relations
  Commission, Board of Library Trustees, Parks & Recreation Commission, Planning
  Commission, Transportation Commission, and Youth Commission with each appointment
  to be effective for a period commencing March 23, 2026 and ending March 22, 2027. Other
  than announcing names of new appointees, no action was required.

 4.  DRAFT COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN AND PUBLIC
  REVIEW PERIOD– F2M22-64
  Mayor MALONEY briefly discussed the background of the item, noted that it was made
  possible due to the City receiving a grant of federal funds at the behest of
  Congressmember Judy Chu, and expressed appreciation. Sustainability Analyst MARTEL
  delivered a staff report, Amanda MURRAY from Environmental Science Associates (ESA)
  and Paul PENINGER from BAE Urban Economics delivered a PowerPoint presentation
  which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. At the direction of the City Council, City staff and
  consultants from ESA have developed a Draft Comprehensive Environmental
  Sustainability Plan (the Draft Plan) to provide a long-term framework that will help improve
  environmental and sustainability issues within Alhambra. The Draft Plan strove to balance
  the needs of today's generation with future generations while ensuring a balance for
  economic prosperity, environmental care, and social wellbeing. This presentation provided
  an overview of the Draft Plan, a summary of outreach highlights to date, and a community
  engagement strategy for the public comment period. Staff requested comments on next
  steps for the completion of the document, including releasing the Draft Plan for a public
  comment period to inform the final version of the Plan.

  Public Comment:
  1) Sawyer BROOKS, via Zoom, expressed support for the Plan and requested
  clarification regarding the development of the Streetlight Masterplan.

  2) Jeffrey GOMEZ, 115 Meridian, supported the draft Plan as a member of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission and discussed the Commission’s
  excitement to begin reviewing the Plan.
  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the involvement of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission and public outreach with Ms. MURRAY. They
  also discussed ESA’s work with Los Angeles County Heat Action Plan. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER discussed the use of solar panels, requested more information from Los
  Angeles County for low-income grant assistance, and highlighted the need for continued
  outreach in multiple languages. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. MARTEL discussed
  continued Pop-Up events, such as the Certified Farmer’s Market and the upcoming Peeps
  and Pedals event. They also discussed resident’s involvement with Clean Power Alliance
  and grant possibilities for low-income residents. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER encouraged
  staff to reach out to environmental students at Alhambra High School for input or
  involvement.
  Councilmember WANG referred to Mr. Brook’s comments regarding the Streetlight Master
  Plan, further coordination with the Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, discussed the importance
  of family engagement, and continued to discuss ongoing community engagement and
  input with Ms. MURRAY. Ms. WANG also discussed the town hall events and providing
  information to the public regarding the progress of the Plan. She questioned if Council
  would prefer to combine the five upcoming town hall meetings into one in order to more
  efficiently proceed with the Plan’s development. Councilmember MAZA also discussed
  streetlights and the use of solar powered street lights.

  Councilmember LEE discussed rising food prices and the use of the Alhambra Community
  Garden. She proposed staff find a location for a second community garden to assist
  renters who may not have room for a home garden and stressed the need to address
  food insecurity. Ms. MARTEL provided clarification regarding public input and existing
  programs with the library. Ms. LEE requested Council consider a mini-grant program to
  assist the City promote the Sustainability Plan programs.

Regular City Council Meeting Minutes — March 23, 2026  Page 4 of 10
   Mayor MALONEY spoke in support of the Plan, the City’s background with sustainability
  programs such as Clean Power Alliance, and the importance of renewable energy
  sources. He went on to discuss the evolution of the Plan and requested continued
  community engagement and regular quarterly updates to the Environmental Sustainability
  Plan. He agreed with Ms. Wang’s suggestion to merge the five meetings into one large in
  person and one Zoom meeting. He also suggested continued outreach on the City’s social
  media.

  Action Taken:  City Council received an overview of the Draft Comprehensive
  Environmental Sustainability Plan; and, directed staff to release the Draft Plan for a period
  of public review and provided comments to Staff.

5.  RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A CITY-WIDE COMMEMORATIVE HISTORIC PLAQUE
  PROGRAM – F2M26-30, R2M26-6

  The Director of Community Development presented a staff report reviewing the
  development of the City’s Comprehensive Historic Preservation Program, it was planned
  to include a Voluntary Commemorative Historic Plaque Program to recognize historic
  resources. Staff and the consultant, Historic Resources Group (HRG), researched other
  programs and presented findings to the Historic Preservation Commission (HPC).

  Public Comment:
  1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., suggested additional informational historic
  plaques throughout the City.

  2) Brian OTIS requested additional educational plaques and historic plaques noting
  former residences of famous people in Alhambra.
  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE supported the program and discussed the
  cost of the program to the owner with Mr. HO. They continued to discuss the
  implementation of the program, similar programs in other cities, and the value to the
  homeowner in participating in the program. Councilmember MAZA supported the program
  and discussed the wording as developed by the Historic Resource Survey with Mr. HO.
  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. HO discussed the eligible homes who could
  purchase the plaque at the expense of the homeowner. Mayor MALONEY supported the
  program and referred to comments regarding additional historic plaques in the City. Mr.
  HO provided clarification. They also discussed people putting up their own plaques.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-6 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, establishing a City-Wide
  Commemorative Historic Plaque Program

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, LEE, MAZA, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE
